key_insight: Competing Ge-driven polar off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature phase boundary at 60–65% Sn in lead-free CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃.
engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn mixing offers a route to tune polar order, octahedral rotations, and band gaps in lead-free halide perovskites.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across the full Ge/Sn composition range.
Map temperature-dependent phases, structural distortions, and band-gap trends.
evidence_signal: The simulated phase diagram reproduces reported transition sequences and temperatures for both end members and predicts an intermediate I4/mcm phase near the alloy boundary.
watch_item: The predicted alloy phase boundary and intermediate phase require experimental validation; agreement for the end members alone does not establish alloy accuracy.
paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
